notes: Sourced from the live 'District/Constituency/Member of Legislative Assembly/Remarks' rosters on the main Wikipedia articles for the Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Rajasthan Legislative Assemblies (fetched 2026-09-25), which are maintained as running compositions (district, constituency, current party+member, remarks) and already fold in by-elections, deaths, resignations and defections, cross-checked constituency-by-constituency against each table's rowspan history so the *current* occupant (not the original 2023 winner) is recorded. All three assemblies are unicameral (no Vidhan Parishad), so no MLC positions apply. Election result (counting) date for all three states was 2023-12-03 (MP polled 2023-11-17, Chhattisgarh in two phases 2023-11-07/17, Rajasthan 2023-11-25); used as `since` for members never replaced. Confirmed by-election replacements since the 2023 election: MP Vijaypur (INC->INC, Mukesh Malhotra, 2024-11-23), MP Amarwara ST (INC->BJP defector Kamlesh Shah re-won as BJP, dated 2024-11-23 — exact counting day inferred from the same nationwide 23 Nov 2024 bypoll round as the other seats below since the constituency page only cites an ECI result-page date of 25 Nov 2024, hence confidence=medium on that one seat), MP Budhni (BJP->BJP, Ramakant Bhargava after Shivraj Singh Chouhan's move to Lok Sabha, 2024-11-23), Chhattisgarh Raipur City South (BJP->BJP, Sunil Kumar Soni after Brijmohan Agrawal's resignation, 2024-11-23), and 9 Rajasthan seats in the 2024-06-04 (Bagidora, BAP), 2024-11-23 (Jhunjhunu, Ramgarh, Dausa, Deoli-Uniara, Khinwsar, Salumber, Chorasi) and 2025-11-14 (Anta, disqualification of Kanwar Lal Meena) rounds — all party flips/continuities per the table are as listed in each position's holder.party. Two Rajasthan MLAs (Sadulpur's Manoj Nyangli, Bari's Jaswant Singh Gurjar) are recorded 'Merged With Shiv Sena From BSP' i.e. elected as BSP in 2023 and now sitting as SHS (Shiv Sena, 2022-present/Shinde faction) without a seat change, so `since` stays the 2023 result date for them; a third Rajasthan SHS MLA (Bayana's Ritu Banawat) is recorded the same way. This yields party-wise strength BJP 118 / INC 67 / BAP 4 / SHS 3 / RLD 1 / IND 7 for Rajasthan, vs. BJP 118 / INC 67 / BAP 4 / SHS 2 / IND 8 in the existing states-mp-cg-rj.json snapshot — the 1-seat difference is this extra confirmed BSP->SHS merger; not reconciled with that file, flagging for a cross-segment pass. Investigated and REJECTED an unsourced claim (found as stray, uncited prose appended after the MP members table on Wikipedia, contradicted by Om Prakash Sakhlecha's own bio page which still shows him as sitting/incumbent, and unconfirmed by Bing News) that Jawad MLA Om Prakash Sakhlecha was 'Disqualified on 3 April 2026'; his seat is recorded here as held, not vacant, per the 'never invent, and don't blindly trust an uncited edit either' quality bar — flagged for a follow-up verification pass given it concerns a sitting cabinet minister. No seats found vacant in any of the three assemblies as of fetch time.

verification.method: Re-fetched live wikitext+HTML for the members tables of 16th Rajasthan Assembly, 16th Madhya Pradesh Assembly and 6th Chhattisgarh Assembly (en.wikipedia.org API, independent of the segment's own scrape/build pipeline), independently re-parsed all three tables (handling each table's own column ordering and rowspan-continuation conventions), and diffed all 520 positions 1:1 against the file by normalized constituency name. Also cross-checked the three assembly infoboxes' party-wise seat totals against data/raw/states-mp-cg-rj.json and states-mp-cg-rj-r2.json, and spot-verified the two highest-risk facts (Om Prakash Sakhlecha/Jawad non-disqualification, Anta by-election) against separate Wikipedia bio/constituency pages.
verification.currentHouseConfirmed: All three are the assemblies elected in the 2023 general elections (MP/Chhattisgarh 2023-11, Rajasthan 2023-11-25), still the sitting house as of 2026-09-25 (next elections due 2028, none of the three appear in the 2025-2026 election calendar). Confirmed via each assembly's Wikipedia infobox last_election/leader dates.
verification.byElectionSweep2025_2026: Re-derived from live tables rather than the file's own notes: no MP or Chhattisgarh by-elections found in 2025 or 2026 (last change in both was the Nov 2024 nationwide bypoll round, already reflected). Rajasthan: confirmed the single 2025 change already in the file - Anta (st-rj-pos-mla-anta), Kanwar Lal Meena (BJP) succeeded by Pramod Jain Bhaya (INC) since 2025-11-14 - and found no other 2025/2026 Rajasthan changes. Independently corroborated via the Anta Assembly constituency Wikipedia page.

partyWiseStatsRecomputed.note: No entity stats patches were needed - all three already matched the member-level recount exactly. Flagging a SEPARATE, out-of-scope discrepancy for a future cross-segment pass: data/raw/states-mp-cg-rj.json and states-mp-cg-rj-r2.json both show Rajasthan as SHS 2 / IND 8 (copied from the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly article's summary infobox), but the infobox is stale by one seat - the live row-by-row members table (independently re-parsed here) lists 3 sitting Shiv Sena MLAs (Sadulpur/Manoj Nyangli, Bayana/Ritu Banawat, Bari/Jaswant Singh Gurjar, all 'Merged With Shiv Sena From BSP' or shown as Shiv Sena), so SHS 3 / IND 7 (as already recorded in this file) is the figure supported by the primary member-level data, not the summary infobox.

spotCheck.coverage: 100% (520/520) automated diff against a freshly re-fetched and independently re-parsed Wikipedia members table per house, exceeding the requested 30-member sample.
spotCheck.falsePositiveInvestigated: Rajasthan has two distinct constituencies both literally named 'Shahpura' (Shahpura, Jaipur and Shahpura, Bhilwara); an early pass of the diff script collided the two under one normalized-name key and flagged a false mismatch. Both file positions (st-rj-pos-mla-shahpura-jaipur = Manish Yadav/INC, st-rj-pos-mla-shahpura-bhilwara = Lalaram Bairwa/BJP) were confirmed correct against the corresponding numbered rows (42 and 181) in the live table.
independentSourceChecks: Om Prakash Sakhlecha (Jawad, MP): confirmed still incumbent MLA via his own Wikipedia bio page infobox (status: Incumbent) - upholds the file's rejection of the uncited 'disqualified 3 April 2026' claim.
Anta (RJ): confirmed Pramod Jain Bhaya (INC) is the current MLA via the Anta Assembly constituency Wikipedia page, elected in the 2025 by-election after Kanwar Lal Meena (BJP).
spotCheck.notPerformed: Direct scraping of the official Rajasthan/MP/Chhattisgarh assembly websites or ECI result pages was attempted (curl reached all three official domains) but a scriptable member-list endpoint was not found within this pass's time budget, and this session's WebSearch quota was exhausted by prior work before a broader ECI cross-check could be run. Recommend a follow-up pass hitting rajassembly.rajasthan.gov.in / mpvidhansabha.nic.in / cgvidhansabha.gov.in member-list pages directly.
